content:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent 7-day mean.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +2% above recent 14-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak or use 14-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and model is flat or rising slowly, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast based on sentiment strength.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply 10–15% downward bias to first 7 days if sentiment swings >0.4.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+1.5% above 30-day moving average for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 0.2–0.5% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.3) triggers model lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day sentiment-weighted average, not 30d trend.
